repo_prior_art.cite: none; the Panel catalogue has no survival/censoring spectral-SSC inference result

published_prior_art.cite: HanShah2025SSC supplies SSC identification/finite-sample guarantees, WestlingLuedtkeGilbertCarone2024 supplies one-law orthogonal survival inference, and GolubPereyra1973 supplies the differential; none supplies their three-block composition.
WestlingLuedtkeGilbertCarone2024 supplies feasible survival bands and integrated-contrast inference; the incremental content is propagation through the transported SSC influence vector.

CurthPoonNoriGonzalez2024 studies survival-SC bias and WestlingLuedtkeGilbertCarone2024 distinguishes covariate-adjusted survival targets, but neither derives this three-block KM/PCR probability limit and relatively open nonzero-bias subclass.

ChoiKwonLiao2026RankRobust and FanLiao2022Diversified address high-dimensional diversified-projection/factor regimes, not fixed-panel nonlinear pseudoinverse transport under survival-score noise and local singular collision.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 1 / def:rational-witness
soundness_flags.one_line: P★ is declared a product of five cell laws and constructs only y, M, and B cells, but C contains six cells including the target factual-post cell; specify that sixth law (and its survival pair) before asserting P★ belongs to the full panel submodel.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1–2
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Exact donor-span and post-period donor transport are maintained identification premises, not results derived by this project.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The joint limit law, multiplier band, and grid-RMST interval hold conditional on the exact SSC transport model and fixed positive singular gap; the contribution is inference conditional on that causal transport model.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives SSC identification and finite-sample consistency using Kaplan–Meier cell-error control, row-space transport, and PCR stability under a well-conditioned spectrum.

The paper analyzes distributional/survival-curve bias and dependence induced by synthetic units, then proposes regularization tradeoffs; it does not derive a conditional-censoring three-block PCR probability limit.

source_verification_receipts.version: JASA 121(553), 2026, pp. 655–666; companion arXiv:2311.16440v2 inspected for model description
source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher issue listing and abstract; arXiv v2, Sections 1–2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published work concerns rank-misspecification-robust inference for linear functionals of high-dimensional low-rank matrices using diversified projections, not a fixed-dimensional nonlinear pseudoinverse target.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corroboration; cited JASA full text was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Section 4.2 and proof of asymptotic-linearity theorem
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work develops cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival-curve estimation with pointwise and uniform asymptotic linearity; the exact journal theorem numbering was not used for any adverse flag.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Complete P★ as a six-cell product law by giving the target factual-post cell explicitly, then state its positive risk denominators and verify the displayed Kaplan–Meier/PCR limit from those atom probabilities.
Add a compact boundary corollary showing that the transported influence formula reduces to Han–Shah’s Kaplan–Meier regular case under marginally independent censoring and constant nuisances.
Develop the weak-gap handle into a concrete local experiment with an observable threshold and a stated attainable/impossible subclass, rather than leaving its phase boundary wholly open.

recommended_next_step: Repair the incomplete rational witness, then advance the field-tier conditional inference kernel to Stage 0.
